replacements.old:
For higher zero branches, monotonicity in the deformation parameter is
suggested by the first correction but is proved globally only at $n=1$.
replacements.new:
For higher zero branches, the differentiated concentration theorem in
Chapter~\ref{ch:lerchbd} proves decreasing motion, and negativity of any
fixed finite number of parameter derivatives, once the derivative order is
sufficiently large. An unrestricted all-order statement is false: at first
derivative order the index-two lower branch has one nondegenerate minimum,
and simple first-order endpoint branches have alternating directions.
The complete index-two family has two simple positive zeros for every
$\rho\in[0,1]$ and every derivative order; higher-index weak deformations
can lose real zeros. The unique index-three inner-gap fold is proved,
while possible additional outer folds remain a separate question.
